questions.hint: Divide the larger perimeter by the smaller.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Reason about triangle centers
questions.stem: Which center is the intersection of angle bisectors?

options.text: The orthocenter is the intersection of angle bisectors
The centroid is the intersection of angle bisectors
The circumcenter is the intersection of angle bisectors
The incenter is the intersection of angle bisectors

questions.explanation: The incenter is where angle bisectors meet. The centroid is median intersection, circumcenter is perpendicular bisector intersection, and orthocenter is altitude intersection.
questions.hint: Angle bisectors meet at the incenter.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute area of a triangle
questions.stem: A triangular lot has base 11 m and height 4 m; what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = 0.5 × 11 × 4 = 22 m². A value of 44 would forget the half factor. Height must be perpendicular.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute a missing side in similar triangles
questions.stem: Similar triangles have sides 7 and 14; if the smaller has side 5, what is the larger matching side?
questions.explanation: Scale factor is 14/7 = 2. The larger matching side is 5 × 2 = 10. A value of 2.5 would divide instead of multiply.
